non_blocking: {"category":"error-handling","summary":"video_concat temp-file creation can throw out of execute() instead of returning a ToolResult","failure_scenario":"If tmpdir is unwritable or disk-full, mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),'dsh-ffmpeg-concat-')) or writeFileSync(listPath, ...) throws; the exception propagates as a rejected promise out of execute(), violating the 'always returns a canonical ToolResult' contract. resolveInput/resolveOutput wrap their errors; the concat temp-file path does not."}

{"category":"efficiency","summary":"hasPlaylistSignature performs a synchronous 8 MiB head-read on the Node main thread for every input","failure_scenario":"Every tool call on any regular file opens and reads up to 8 MiB synchronously before ffmpeg runs, blocking the harness event loop for the duration of the disk I/O on each invocation. Bounded, but it is main-thread blocking I/O on the hot path."}

{"category":"correctness","summary":"Clamping -probesize to 8M can break probing of valid media with headers beyond 8 MiB","failure_scenario":"A non-faststart MP4 whose moov atom sits beyond the first 8 MiB (large files without faststart) will no longer be detected by ffmpeg/ffprobe because the probe window is capped at 8M; the tool returns a confusing parse/failure instead of probing the file."}

{"category":"correctness","summary":"Playlist content-signature guard can false-positive on legitimate binary media containing the ASCII markers","failure_scenario":"A valid MP4/JPEG/WAV whose first 8 MiB happen to contain the byte sequences '<mpd', '#extinf', '#extm3u', or '<smoothstreamingmedia' (e.g., embedded XML metadata) is rejected as a manifest even though it is not one."}

{"category":"concurrency","summary":"Overwrite guard is racy across concurrent tool calls to the same output path","failure_scenario":"Two concurrent write calls with the same non-existent output both pass existsSync; the first creates the file, the second's ffmpeg fails with -n and the user sees an opaque 'Output file exists' ToolFailure rather than a canonical result. No corruption, but the guard's messaging depends on child-process timing."}

{"category":"error-handling","summary":"Timed-out writes leave a partial output file that blocks later retries without overwrite=true","failure_scenario":"If ffmpeg is killed at the 300s timeout, the partially-written output remains in the workspace; a subsequent call without overwrite=true refuses to run, and the corrupt file must be manually removed."}

{"category":"correctness","summary":"firstErrorLine surfaces only the first non-empty stderr line","failure_scenario":"Multiline ffmpeg errors (e.g., 'Invalid data found...' followed by a more specific line) are truncated to the first line, losing actionable detail in the model-facing message."}
security: {"category":"credential-redaction-bypass","summary":"redactCredentials fails to redact userinfo containing '/' or a second '@'","failure_scenario":"stderr/stdout containing 'http://user:pa/ss@host' is returned verbatim (both regexes stop at '/'), and 'http://user:p@ss@host' becomes 'http://***@ss@host', leaking 'ss'. A workspace filename with a credential-style name is echoed back to the model partially unredacted."}

{"category":"prompt-injection-surface","summary":"ffprobe format.tags/stream.tags are returned verbatim to the model in raw","failure_scenario":"A hostile media file can carry attacker-controlled text in metadata tags (e.g., a 'comment' tag containing instructions); media_probe serializes the full ffprobe JSON into the model-visible raw without stripping or marking tag fields as untrusted data."}

{"category":"toctou","summary":"Playlist-signature guard is not atomic with ffmpeg's open of the input","failure_scenario":"A file swapped between the 8 MiB signature check and ffmpeg/ffprobe opening it (concurrent writer in the workspace) is dereferenced by ffmpeg, whose -protocol_whitelist still permits file:; local file:// references in the swapped-in playlist are read. Residual risk is documented, but the guard can be raced deterministically under concurrent workspace writes."}

{"category":"load-bearing-assumption","summary":"Env-allowlist safety depends entirely on core's runner applying DEFAULT_ENV_ALLOWLIST when no env is passed","failure_scenario":"runBinary passes no env to ctx.run, trusting that core's runProcess substitutes an allowlist. If that default ever changes to inherit the parent environment, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and other harness secrets reach ffmpeg/ffprobe while they parse untrusted media. A test against runProcess verifies today's behavior, but the plugin is not defensively explicit."}

{"category":"supply-chain","summary":"CI action FedericoCarboni/setup-ffmpeg@v3 is pinned to a mutable major tag","failure_scenario":"A compromised v3 tag release of the action would execute attacker-controlled code on CI runners; pinning to a commit SHA would remove the mutable-tag supply-chain surface."}
test_gaps: {"category":"missing-assertion","summary":"No test asserts -probesize (PROBE_WINDOW) is passed on every invocation","failure_scenario":"The protocol_whitelist test checks file,pipe,fd only; a regression dropping the -probesize clamp would silently widen ffmpeg's auto-detection window beyond the guard's 8 MiB scan."}

{"category":"missing-path","summary":"exec.truncated and timedOut/aborted result paths are untested","failure_scenario":"The 20 MiB output-cap ToolFailure and the Timeout branches in runBinary have no direct test; a regression there would surface malformed results instead of normalized errors."}

{"category":"missing-assertion","summary":"No test asserts tool-specific argv construction","failure_scenario":"video_clip (-ss/-t/-c copy order), media_compress (-crf <default 28>), audio_extract (-vn/-c:a), audio_convert (-c:a), and thumbnail_generate (-vframes 1) are exercised only via the shared -n/-y capture, not their actual argument vectors."}

{"category":"missing-assertion","summary":"Directory-as-input rejection is untested; the non-regular-file check is only exercised by the POSIX FIFO test","failure_scenario":"A directory input path that slips past resolveInWorkspace would reach ffmpeg and behave unpredictably; the isFile() rejection branch has no coverage on Windows (where the FIFO test skips)."}

{"category":"test-isolation","summary":"The FIFO test permanently replaces the photo.mp4 fixture with a FIFO in the shared workspace","failure_scenario":"After the POSIX FIFO test runs, photo.mp4 in workspaceRoot is a FIFO; any later test or integration run using that fixture fails on the non-regular-file rejection, making the suite order-dependent."}

{"category":"missing-integration","summary":"Real-binary playlist rejection is not tested (guard exercised only with mocks)","failure_scenario":"The signature-guard alignment with ffmpeg's actual probe behavior (window size, marker scan) is asserted only against mocked ExecutionResults; a real .m3u8/.mpd probe against installed ffmpeg would validate the claim end-to-end."}

{"category":"missing-assertion","summary":"Redaction tests do not cover the known '/' / second-'@' bypass or scheme-less user:pass@","failure_scenario":"Only 'scheme://user:pass@host' forms are asserted; the partial-redaction cases identified in the security review would pass CI unnoticed."}
compatibility: {"category":"upstream-api-drift","summary":"Core API surface (assertPermission, resolveInWorkspace, WorkspaceViolationError, parseJsonOutput, validateArgs, permission-object shape) must match the pinned upstream commit","failure_scenario":"The compatibility manifest itself marks permission_hook_api as 'TBD — must be verified'; in-monorepo typecheck/build passing proves nothing about the pinned deepseek-harness commit, so a mismatch would fail at integration time rather than at review time."}

{"category":"core-default-env","summary":"The security claim 'harness secrets never reach ffmpeg' depends on core's default env-allowlist behavior being stable","failure_scenario":"If core's runner changes to pass the inherited environment when env is omitted, this plugin silently inherits full env without any code change — a compatibility coupling that is load-bearing for the security model."}

{"category":"contract-version","summary":"metadata.coreContractVersion ('0.1.0') must equal core's CORE_VERSION","failure_scenario":"Relies entirely on the contract test kit to catch drift; if core bumps CORE_VERSION, this plugin fails the shared suite until the field is updated."}
architecture: {"category":"infrastructure-duplication","summary":"binary.ts reimplements binary detection (PATH scan + missing-sentinel) instead of using core's binary-detection facility","failure_scenario":"The Plugin Standard requires binary detection to come from @dsh-forge/core; the external-security-review invariants (never bare name, unpredictable sentinel) may justify a custom resolver, but reuse of core's resolver should be confirmed or the deviation justified in the PR."}

{"category":"naming-convention","summary":"Tool names use semantic prefixes (media_, video_, audio_, thumbnail_) rather than the tool-family prefix convention","failure_scenario":"The standard's examples (ast_search, ruff_check) prefix with the upstream tool family; media_probe/video_clip/audio_convert are not ffmpeg-prefixed, creating potential name-collision space with other plugins' tools."}

{"category":"duplication","summary":"video_concat duplicates runWrite's permission/resolve/execute flow inline","failure_scenario":"The concat tool hand-rolls the same permission check, overwrite guard, protocol_whitelist/probesize header, and error mapping as runWrite; the two paths can diverge on future security hardening (e.g., a new global flag added to one but not the other)."}
